BLOCK - performance, pr:301, round 1 of at most 2.

R301-P1 - MEDIUM - retained templates are not byte-bounded.
Location: crates/cli/src/daemon_log.rs:534-542 (stored in Seen at 546-551).
String::from_utf8_lossy(...).into_owned() allocates the full template. truncate(end) changes its length, not its capacity, and pushing the ellipsis reuses that allocation. The 256-entry limit therefore retains O(256 * input-line length), not the claimed approximately 80 KB. This is newly retained memory: distinct, never-repeated templates have no timer and can stay in the map indefinitely while the daemon is quiet. The existing reader explicitly accepts long lines.

Repro: on an unchanged copy of this head's daemon_log.rs, construct Repeats::new(REPEAT_WINDOW, REPEAT_KEYS); admit 256 lines at one Instant, each with a distinct two-letter ASCII prefix and 32,768 'x' bytes; sum seen.values().map(|s| s.shown.capacity()). The nice19 exact-source probe returned 256 keys, 62,208 displayed bytes, but 8,389,376 retained String-capacity bytes alone (8.0007 MiB), before Seen/map overhead. Every first line was admitted; this does not depend on an attacker, a hash collision or an exotic launcher. A 240-byte shown-template limit does not establish the memory bound.

Required fix: store a bounded owned summary allocation (or release the excess allocation before inserting), without truncating the full template used for the hash. Add a focused regression inspecting retained storage, not only the returned summary's length. This is a cost-bound correctness finding in round 1, not an availability block.

Cost otherwise acceptable:
- Work is driven by log input, not a tick or a seat. The two reader threads and shared serialization already existed. Added repeat admission does an O(line bytes) digit-template pass and explicit DefaultHasher, followed by HashMap hashing/lookup; it is not literally just one hash operation. Up to 256 entries are visited on due-window sweeps or capacity eviction. Different staggered windows can require separate sweeps; "once per window" is not one sweep for the entire daemon per minute.
- pump arms SO_RCVTIMEO only after the shared repeats.counting() state becomes true, and removes it when observed false. The timeout is 60 s of read inactivity, not an exact deadline timer; incoming complete lines also flush due windows. At most one idle timeout per 60 s per armed stream (two streams); no per-seat scaling, no process launches. Existing timer/reader tests passed.
- Optimized, exact-source, nice19 probe, median of five 200,000-admission runs: 156-byte bg lines 137.1 ns/line; 184-byte pane lines 152.5 ns/line. 512-template capacity churn: 1,441.1 ns/line. Shared distinct-line handling to /dev/null, including timestamps/writes: 2,471.8 ns/line. These are isolated core measurements, not a deployed CPU forecast or full reader benchmark.
- One-hour replay using the committed burst payloads/rates and actual Shared sink: background 36,000 input lines, 6,624,000 timestamped bytes before, 26,030 bytes after; pane 6,000 input lines, 1,272,000 before, 29,384 after. Each produced 120 physical lines (60 first occurrences and 60 summaries). Historical fleet frequency and steady-state averages are author receipts, not independently re-read live logs.
- Normal rotation shifts two numbered files, renames current to .1, and renames the staged fresh file to current: four renames plus one create/open at 16 MiB, not three renames. It does not copy the log. Scratch probe: 100 rotations averaged 922.3 us. Oversized 40 MiB startup log: retained 16,777,200 bytes in 21.704 ms. Cached-file timings, no fsync/device-durability claim. No live log touched.
- Size retention and startup trimming are DESTRUCTIVE POLICIES, not brakes. The identity guard only vetoes adoption. Correctness/security of crash, concurrent launchers and path races belongs to their independent roles.
- No production launch site was added. spawn_sites passed all six tests, including counted sites and widened bare-name controls. N1 is comment-only; the lsof documentation now charges one per ancestry proof, including two when both proofs run. N2 remains a lexical tripwire for its supported source forms, not Rust-wide dataflow proof; the inherited resolver can still return a bare miss or a relative PATH hit, so a launch-closure parameter is not itself proof of an absolute runtime path.
